I can’t keep watching the page in the background from here. However, I can help you set up an automated monitor that will notify you the instant the status goes red and produce a summary of the hour afterward. Pick one of the options below (or tell me the status-page URL and preferred notification channel and I’ll tailor the setup):

Options
- I create a small script you can run on your machine/VM (polls the status page every 30–60s, sends a Slack/Email/desktop notification if it detects "red", and writes logs for a one-hour summary).
- I show how to configure a monitoring service (UptimeRobot / Pingdom / PagerDuty / Statuspage webhooks / IFTTT) to send instant alerts and keep history for a summary.
- I poll it for you manually right now (one-shot check and snapshot). I cannot stay connected continuously after this message.

If you want the script, tell me:
- the status-page URL (or the vendor name if they use a common provider like Statuspage.io)
- which notification method you prefer (Slack webhook, SMS, email, desktop notification)
- how often you want polling (I recommend 30–60 seconds; be mindful of rate limits)
- what you mean by “red” (if you know the exact status value, e.g., "major_outage"; otherwise I’ll assume typical mapping: green = operational, degraded = degraded_performance/partial_outage, red = major_outage)

Example (ready-to-run) — Linux/macOS bash + Slack webhook
- Requirements: curl, jq, a Slack Incoming Webhook URL
- Replace STATUS_URL and SLACK_WEBHOOK, then run. It will:
  - poll every 30s
  - send a Slack message the first time status becomes "red"
  - log timestamps/status to monitor.log for the 1-hour summary

#!/usr/bin/env bash
STATUS_URL="https://your-vendor.statuspage.io/api/v2/status.json"  # replace
SLACK_WEBHOOK="https://hooks.slack.com/services/XXX/YYY/ZZZ"       # replace
INTERVAL=30
END_TIME=$((SECONDS + 3600))
alerted=0
echo "start_time=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")" > monitor.log

while [ $SECONDS -lt $END_TIME ]; do
  response=$(curl -s --fail "$STATUS_URL")
  if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ") ERROR fetching" >> monitor.log
    sleep $INTERVAL
    continue
  fi

  # example for Statuspage.io: .status.description or .status.indicator
  status=$(echo "$response" | jq -r '.status.indicator // .status.description // empty')
  timestamp=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
  echo "$timestamp $status" >> monitor.log

  # consider "major" or "major_outage" as red — adjust if needed
  if [[ "$status" =~ major|down|red|major_outage ]]; then
    if [ $alerted -eq 0 ]; then
      alerted=1
      curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-type: application/json' \
        --data "{\"text\":\"ALERT: status went RED at $timestamp — status: $status\"}" \
        "$SLACK_WEBHOOK" >/dev/null
      echo "$timestamp ALERT_SENT" >> monitor.log
    fi
  fi

  sleep $INTERVAL
done

# After hour: produce a short summary
echo "end_time=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")" >> monitor.log
echo "Summary:" > summary.txt
echo "Monitoring window: $(head -n1 monitor.log | cut -d'=' -f2) to $(tail -n1 monitor.log | cut -d'=' -f2)" >> summary.txt
echo "" >> summary.txt
echo "Status timeline (timestamp status):" >> summary.txt
grep -v '^start_time' monitor.log >> summary.txt
# you can cat summary.txt or send via webhook/email

Notes and cautions
- Many status pages expose a JSON API (e.g., Statuspage.io /api/v2/status.json). If yours does, using the API makes parsing reliable. If not, the script may need minimal HTML scraping.
- Don’t poll too frequently (30s–60s suggested) to avoid hitting rate limits.
- If you want SMS, I can add Twilio example; for email I can show sendmail/SMTP.
- If you want a hosted solution (UptimeRobot/Pingdom/PagerDuty), I can give step-by-step setup and link a webhook to Slack/SMS and produce downloadable logs for your summary.

Next step
Reply with the status page URL and your preferred notification method (Slack/email/SMS/desktop), and I’ll give the exact script or the service configuration and a ready-to-run summary template.
